AK.key_factor: Peltola led the all-party primary and leads late first-choice polls by enough that ranked-choice transfers from two minor Republicans may not catch her.
AK.reasoning: Sullivan can still gain when Heikes and Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. are eliminated, and the late spoiler investigation is a real risk. Alaska Survey Research, Siena and polls from both parties nonetheless have her ahead on first choices, and she has far more money. That is a narrow final-round win.

FL.key_factor: Moody leads by about five points in almost every poll in a state Trump carried by 13.
FL.reasoning: Nixon's fundraising and the national climate have tightened a race Rubio won by 16, and early ballots are roughly balanced by party. Florida's registration advantage, Election Day Republican vote and Nixon's democratic-socialist profile still leave the appointed incumbent clearly ahead.

IA.key_factor: The public polling average is a dead heat, and Libertarian Thomas Laehn pulls more from Hinson than from Turek.
IA.reasoning: Iowa voted Republican by 13 points in 2024, and several Republican polls still have Hinson up one or two. Marist, Suffolk and YouGov have Turek ahead, Democrats have spent far more, and this is an open seat. I take Turek in a photo finish.

KS.key_factor: Late polls from Emerson, The Washington Post and CNN all show Hamilton ahead of the incumbent.
KS.reasoning: Kansas is solidly Republican, but it ticket-splits and Hamilton has raised far more than Marshall. Republican polls show a tie, not a Marshall lead. Marshall's patient-lawsuit record and a damaging closing rally make this the rare red state where the challenger is actually ahead.

ME.key_factor: Since October Collins has been tied or behind in nearly every survey, including Republican polls, in a state Trump has never carried.
ME.reasoning: Collins beat a similar polling deficit in 2020, so a two-point Jackson lead is not safe. This time the evidence is broader, Trump's approval is much weaker, and only two candidates are on the ballot, so ranked-choice voting will not decide it. I side narrowly with the polls.

MI.key_factor: El-Sayed leads by roughly four points across Republican, Democratic and university polls, against a nominee who just lost here.
MI.reasoning: He is more progressive than Slotkin, who beat this same Republican by 0.3 points in 2024, and GOP groups are spending heavily to stop him. The state was only barely Republican for president, the midterm climate has moved it, and his campaign has far more money than Rogers.

MN.key_factor: Flanagan leads every recent poll, including Tafoya's own campaign survey and Republican firms.
MN.reasoning: She is the sitting lieutenant governor in a state Democrats carried for president in 2024. Siena's 14-point margin is probably too wide, but SurveyUSA, Mason-Dixon and the GOP polls all show the same winner. Tafoya's money keeps the race from becoming a landslide.

NC.key_factor: Cooper, a two-term governor, leads a former party chair by high single digits in every poll, including Republican surveys.
NC.reasoning: Whatley is stuck near 42 percent. University polls and Quantus, Trafalgar and Harper agree. Senate Republican spending was pulled back, Cooper has much more cash, and he has already won statewide while Republicans carried North Carolina for president.

NE.key_factor: Osborn's own October pollster still has him trailing in a state Trump won by 20 points.
NE.reasoning: Osborn came within seven points of Fischer in 2024, no Democrat is splitting the ballot, and outside spending favors him. YouGov has him up a point. Republican surveys and his campaign's numbers still show the former governor ahead, so I keep Ricketts by a small margin.

NH.key_factor: Pappas leads by 5 to 8 points in every post-primary poll, including Saint Anselm, UNH and Republican pollsters.
NH.reasoning: The Sununu name and heavy Republican outside spending keep the race short of safe. John E. Sununu has not won an election in years, remains stuck in the mid-40s, and was heavily outspent by Pappas's own campaign in a slightly Democratic state.

OH.key_factor: Brown leads most late polls by 2 to 5 points, two years after losing Ohio's other Senate race by only 3.6.
OH.reasoning: The state has moved right, Husted is a known statewide official, and a few Republican polls show a tie. Brown's lead matches a midterm correction of that 2024 loss, and he has raised more than three times as much. I give him a close race.

SC.key_factor: An appointed incumbent still leads in East Carolina, Trafalgar and Rasmussen surveys in a state Trump carried by 18 points.
SC.reasoning: Graham won a narrow runoff, has raised very little, and is tied in the Siena poll, so Andrews has a real path. Undecided voters in South Carolina lean Republican, and most nonpartisan and Republican polls still have Graham in front by a few points.

TX.key_factor: Talarico leads or ties in most October polls while Republican outside groups have barely spent to defend Paxton.
TX.reasoning: Texas last elected a Democratic senator decades ago, and statewide polls have often missed toward Republicans, so a one-point edge is fragile. Paxton's impeachment, the rejection of Cornyn, and Talarico's huge money advantage are enough to overcome an R+14 state by a hair.

upset_watch.why: Hinson is the closest trailing candidate: an open seat in a state Trump carried by 13, with polls inside the margin of error and a Libertarian who may fade.
